content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a Deep Image Dependency based full reference Image quality access model, by introducing Brownian Distance Covariance, which is invariant to translation and orthonormal transformations. The Image quality is evaluated upon the BDC upon the deep feature obtained from the VGG pretrained backbone. As the result, the feature dependency facilitates the comparisons of deep learning features in a high-order manner with Brownian distance covariance, which is characterized by the joint distribution of the features from reference and test images, as well as their marginal distributions. Experiments are conducted on image quality prediction, texture image similarity, and geometric invariance to validate the performance of our proposed metric.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
+  This paper apply Brownian Distance Covariance of the deep feature of distorted images to predict the image quality with full reference. 
+ The proposed method could tackle both linear and non-linear transformation and solve the IQA from the aspect of feature distribution, and outperform the other feature based IQA methods.
+ Extensive experiments have been conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed DID model.
Weakness:
- In section 3, the proposed scheme chooses cosine similarity instead of inner product to measure the feature dependency. But in Xie’s work, inner product outperforms the cosine similarity. Is this design difference caused by the different goals?
- The formulation of the methods should be refined. Some symbols are repeated used but with different meaning. For example, the p, q are frequently used as dimension of the vectors. Meanwhile, they are also used as prediction and quality factor. The t,s in equation(7) denoted the component to be integrated, and in the properity (iii), they are used as constant vectors and numbers.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is well organized. The Brownian Distance Covariance has been proposed and used in few shot learning. This paper applies BDC to IQA task and enables a new way to measure the distortion level in terms of deep feature dependency.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The authors have proposed a deep image dependency based FR IQA model that adopts the Brownian distance covariance to mearsure the comparisons of deep learning features. The model is effective for generative images and delivers comptetitive performance as compared with several IQA algorithms.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength :
The authors deploy the Brownian distance covariance for modeling feature dependency.
Weaknesses:
1)	The novelty is limited. The paper only deploys the Brownian distance covariance as the feature dependency measure for FR IQA.
2)	The motivation of the proposed model is not clear, such as the motivation for modeling the texture variation by feature dependency measure.
3)	Some traditional distance-based FR-IQA models still use statistical features. And the deficiency analysis of distance-based methods mentioned in this paper is only for generating images. I suggest the authors add a comprehensive analysis of the distance-based and dependency-based models.
4)	In Section 1, "human perception is usually invariant to the texture resampling…" lacks support materials.
5)	In Section 3.1, the formula is wrong in “(iii) For all constant vector....”
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is clear, but all components of the model are not original and lack high quality contributions.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
The authors propose a new descriptor of subjective image quality when the original and the distorted pictures are available (the full reference situation). The descriptor is based on a measure of the statistical dependence of the features of both images in the inner representation of image classification networks.
The proposed descriptor is well correlated with human opinion in general-purpose image quality databases, successfully predicts subjective similarity of textures, and (similarly to humans) is invariant to small geometric transformations of the images such as rotations, translations, scalings, as well as to texture resampling via deep models.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
* Strength: the best part of the work is the good empirical performance of the proposed metric, but this good feature is not properly explained in the current text.

Weaknesses include the following:

* The "paradigm shift" and the "new design philosophy" claimed in the title/abstract/conclusion (from distance to dependence) is not justified by the actual expressions behind the proposal, that in the end (Eq. 9) reduce to subtractions (i.e. distances) between image representations. The authors should specify which part of Szekely & Rizzo 09 justifies that comparison of charasteristic functions reduce to subtractions of variables.

* The current literature review reveals a confusion of the authors on core concepts because some previous work has already criticised deterministic computation of differences and proposed to change the focus to statistical similarity as opposed to deterministic proximity. This applies to SSIM and variants, VIF, and more recently to DISTS. The approaches based on style similarity (Gatys et al.) go in the same direction because they compute similarities between covariance matrices. Therefore, I think the authors should tone down the "paradigm shift" claim in the title/text and rewrite the introduction to avoid this confusion.
I think the authors should remove the two "knowledge-driven" and "data-driven" categories in the introduction because they interfere with (more meaningful) categories such as (1) "visibility of differences" or "distance" versus (2) "statistical similarity/dissimilarity". 
The "visibility of distance" should include (on top of the naive MSE):

. Ahumada NASA 1993 lists the seminal works that propose differences in the inner representation of the human visual system

. Teo and Heeger IEEE ICIP 1994

. Malo et al. Image Vision Computing 1997

. Laparra et al. JOSA A 2010

. Laparra et al. Electr. Imag. 2016, NLPD is just the automatic differentiation fit of a simplified version of Laparra et al. 2010

. Zhang et al. CVPR 2018 LPIPS which uses the differences and fits the net to maximize correlation

. Hepburn et al. IEEE ICIP 2020 which constraints the net architecture and nonlinearities using the knowledge of visual system

On the other hand, the "statistical similarity" should include:

. Wang and Simoncelli IEEE TIP 2004 (SSIM)

. Sheik et al. IEEE TIP 2006 (VIF) 

. Ding et al. IEEE PAMI 2020 (DISTS)

. Kligvasser et al. NeurIPS 21 which uses the similarity of Gram matrices

. Liao et al. ACM Mutimed. 2022 (DeepWSD)

The proposal of the authors is just another favour of the "statistical similarity" methods, with the advantage (that is true) that it is more invariant to geometrical distortions and texture resampling. But definitely not a "paradigm shift".

* The authors say that their approach has no trainable parameters but this is not strictly true. In fact the statistical comparison is done in the inner representation of certain networks that have been trained for some visual purposes. The performance does not change much depending on the network (VGG, ResNet, and DenseNet), but it is always necessary to be far from the image domain (deep layers) to get an appropriate correlation with human opinion. Therefore, the proposal critically depends on training a sensible representation. This has to be acknowledged, and the role of the representation should be stressed (and explained!).
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
* Notation is not very clear. Some examples: 

. In the definitions of A and B (in Eqs. 8 and 9) the averages over the dimensions are not clear.

. [at the beginning of section 3.2] why x and y belong to R^3 ?

. what does it mean "removing the training sesion for the texture similarity in DISTS_s"?

* Quality: correlation results are competitive but the manuscript does not explain why using these measures leads to these good correlations in those (different) representations. Where the invariance to transformations comes from?

* Novelty: the "paradigm shift" claim is not true: many works (see above) proposed statistical similarity measures before.                    

* Reproducibility: I missed the links to the code.
content.summary_of_the_review:
I think the manuscript cannot be accepted in its current form because it suggests that the authors propose a philosophy which actually was proposed long ago. They should correct these mistake not to mislead the reader.
On the other hand, the work should explain why the proposed measure does acheive the reported invariance to geometrical transformations or resampling better than similar statistical descriptions like DISTS or the differences in Gram matrices in style transfer like methods. 
The proposed descriptor is sensible in certain representations (but not in others) but this issue is not addressed in the work.

content.title: From Distance to Dependency: A Paradigm Shift of Full-reference Image Quality Assessment
content.TL;DR: Beyond distance measure, we propose the first Deep Image Dependency (DID) based full-reference image quality assessment model to capture transformation-invariant  texture perception.
content.abstract: Deep learning-based full-reference image quality assessment (FR-IQA) models typically rely on the feature distance between the reference and distorted images. However, the underlying assumption of these models that the distance in the deep feature domain could quantify the quality degradation does not scientifically align with the invariant texture perception, especially when the images are generated artificially by neural networks.  In this paper, we bring a radical shift in inferring the quality with learned features and propose the Deep Image Dependency (DID) based FR-IQA model.  The feature dependency facilitates the comparisons of deep learning features in a high-order manner with Brownian distance covariance, which is characterized by the joint distribution of the features from reference and test images, as well as their marginal distributions. This enables the quantification of the feature dependency against nonlinear transformation, which is far beyond the computation of the numerical errors in the feature space. Experiments on image quality prediction, texture image similarity, and geometric invariance validate the appealing performance of our proposed measure, and the implementation will be publicly available.
